title: InsightScoop Overview
body:
InsightScoop provides tech-enabled pet waste removal with a free pet wellness app.
- Standard cadence options: Daily (Mon-Fri with optional weekend upgrade for Sat+Sun), Twice-weekly, Weekly, Biweekly, Monthly, or One-time service.
- Field teams double-bag waste with biodegradable liners, capture proof-of-service photos (including gate re-latch), and log 3C health notes after every visit.
- Scooping customers receive pro-assisted wellness with consistent auto-captures from our patent-pending capture device; the app works without the device too.
- Service area focus: Minneapolis metro (South Minneapolis, Richfield, Edina, Bloomington) with nearby suburbs evaluated on request.
- No long-term contracts; cadence and service pauses are flexible with a quick heads-up.
- Sales: sales@yardura.com | Urgent field issues: 1-855-927-3872.

title: Wellness App (Free + Premium)
body:
The InsightScoop app is free for pet owners and provides stool capture with AI summaries (what it could mean), hydration score, firmness scale, and a watch/monitor/vet-now indicator. It also includes weekly check-ins, symptom-aware chat with red-flag tips (not a diagnosis), dog profiles, reminders, food and med logs with ingredient scans and a wellness score, a stool library, vet-ready PDF reports, privacy controls, weather safety alerts, parasite risk calendar, and a poop map that shows location trends.
Premium wellness is $19.99 per month (billed through the app stores on iOS) and adds unlimited scans and chat, long-term trends, early warnings, multi-dog households and family sharing, GPS walk tracking, and a wellness risk score.
Scooping customers get pro-assisted wellness with consistent auto-captures and a pro-verified timeline.

title: Why Owners and Properties Choose InsightScoop
body:
Key differentiators to highlight on calls.
- Background-checked scoopers with QA-reviewed visits and photo confirmation.
- Patent-pending capture device for consistent stool imagery and pro-assisted wellness when scooping is active.
- Free wellness app that turns quick stool captures into easy-to-read insights.
- Flexible scheduling with no long-term contracts and transparent visit logs.
- Eco-friendly practices with optional haul-away or compost routing.

title: Wellness Insights and Disclaimers
body:
Wellness monitoring layers onto every service visit or app capture.
- Scoopers log the 3C rubric (color, consistency, content) and the app adds hydration and firmness scoring.
- The app provides watch/monitor/vet-now guidance and red-flag tips, but it is informational only and not a diagnosis.
- Owners can export a one-page PDF report with recent symptoms and stool images for their vet.
- If asked about medical issues, advise seeing a licensed veterinarian.

title: Core Service Menu
body:
Offerings to reference on calls.
- Weekly scoop: crews walk courtyards, dog runs, and green belts in a perimeter-then-grid pattern, double-bagging waste and relatching gates.
- Deodorize and sanitize: plant-based enzyme sprays added to the end of every visit when selected (one-time available for kickoff cleans).
- Waste diversion: choose haul-away or compost routing (we divert as much as partners can accept) with impact reporting.
- Extra dogs and extra areas (front yard, side yard, dog run, fenced area) adjust per-visit pricing.
- Technicians carry PPE, liners, sanitizer, and spare gate hardware so service stays tidy and self-sufficient.

title: Eco Practices
body:
Environmental commitments that matter to communities.
- Biodegradable liners and sealed bags are standard even when waste remains onsite for municipal pickup.
- Diversion options offer either haul-away or compost routing through local partners; metrics show pounds diverted and methane avoided.
- Natural deodorizing avoids harsh chemicals and is safe for turf, synthetic grass, and paws.
- Impact summaries roll into quarterly business reviews so managers can share sustainability wins with residents.

title: Pricing Guidance
body:
How to handle pricing conversations.
- Community/commercial properties always require a custom proposal; never share specific dollar amounts. Collect site details and offer to loop in sales@yardura.com.
- Residential inquiries can be priced by running the quote flow: confirm service ZIP, property type, dog count, yard size, last cleanup, areas to service, cadence, and add-ons (deodorizing, waste diversion, extra dogs, extra areas).
- Premium wellness app subscriptions are billed separately through the app stores on iOS. Scooping service billing is separate.
- After gathering details, use the quote tools to calculate per-visit and monthly pricing and email the same summary the web quote delivers.

title: Operations and QA
body:
Service-level expectations to communicate.
- Visits land inside the agreed window; weather delays trigger proactive rescheduling updates.
- QA review checks proof-of-service photos, gate re-latch, and notes for accuracy.
- Quality misses are addressed within 24 hours or the visit is credited.
- Visit summaries include time on site, bag counts, 3C notes, and photos so customers have documentation.

title: Quick Answers
body:
High-frequency questions.
- Service area: Minneapolis, Richfield, Edina, and Bloomington today; nearby suburbs can be evaluated when you submit a quote.
- App: The wellness app is free to download and works without scooping. Premium adds unlimited scans, multi-dog, trends, and walk tracking.
- Scoopers: We often assign a consistent scooper for ongoing customers, but coverage may vary to keep service reliable.
- Contracts: Month-to-month membership; give us a quick heads-up to skip for maintenance or snow closures.
- Weather: We service in rain and light snow; deep snow or unsafe ice moves to the next available makeup slot.
- Waste bins: Standard plan uses onsite bins; choose haul-away if you want us to remove waste off property.

title: Commercial Quote Flow
body:
How the quote workflow collects information.
- Start at getinsightscoop.com/quote, choose Community Service, and confirm the ZIP is inside our coverage.
- Provide estimated daily dog count, property size (small, medium, large, enterprise), and how long it has been since a professional cleanup.
- Add notes on pet stations, courtyards, turf type, and preferred visit days so routing can be optimized.
- Submit contact name, role, email, and phone; we reply within one business day to confirm scope, schedule a walkthrough if needed, and deliver the proposal.
- Voice assistant: ask the same questions, then run the quote and email the summary so the caller receives what the web flow would send.

title: Escalation Path
body:
Routing guidance when callers need more help.
- Sales or detailed pricing questions: gather basics and hand off to sales@yardura.com for follow-up.
- Operations emergencies (injury, hazardous spill, access issue): warm transfer to 1-855-927-3872.
- Schedule tweaks: log the request and confirm Operations will update the route; same-day adjustments before 8am are usually possible.

title: Objection: Too Expensive
body:
How to handle price concerns.
- Acknowledge: 'I totally understand wanting to make sure the service fits your budget.'
- Value framing: Pricing includes proof-of-service photos and wellness insights that can help owners spot issues earlier.
- Flexibility: Month-to-month with no contract means you can pause anytime for seasonal or budget changes.
- Compare: Most customers find it costs less than hiring help ad hoc, with far more reliability and documentation.
- If still hesitant: Offer every-other-week service or a smaller area to reduce cost.

title: Objection: I Can Do It Myself
body:
Responding to DIY objections.
- Validate: 'That makes sense. Many customers started out doing it themselves.'
- Time value: Most folks underestimate the time, especially in winter or after snowmelt.
- Consistency: We show up on schedule and document every visit, even when life gets busy.
- Wellness angle: Pro captures and 3C notes can help spot issues earlier.
- Trial option: Suggest trying one month with no long-term commitment.

title: Objection: I'm Just Thinking About It
body:
When the caller isn't ready to commit.
- Respect their timing and offer to email the quote.
- Mention seasonality: spring fills fast, so starting sooner keeps options open.
- Ask if there is any specific concern you can clarify now.

title: Objection: We Already Use Someone
body:
Responding to existing service providers.
- Acknowledge and ask if they are fully satisfied.
- Highlight differentiators: wellness insights, proof-of-service photos, and QA review.
- No pressure: month-to-month makes switching easy if they ever need a backup.

title: Objection: I Only Have One Small Dog
body:
Responding to single-dog or small-dog concerns.
- Validate the smaller mess.
- Emphasize that pricing scales by dog count and yard size.
- Suggest every-other-week service to keep costs low if appropriate.
- Mention wellness insights can still be helpful even for one dog.

title: Objection: What About Winter / Weather?
body:
Addressing seasonal and weather concerns.
- We service year-round, rain or shine, when conditions are safe.
- Deep snow or unsafe ice triggers a reschedule at no extra charge.
- Month-to-month means customers can pause in winter and restart anytime.

title: Objection: Payment / Trust Concerns
body:
Building trust around payment and access.
- Payments are processed securely; we do not store full card numbers.
- Per-visit billing charges after each completed service with photo proof.
- Month-to-month means cancel anytime with no fees.
- Transparency: every visit has photos, bag counts, and notes.

title: Objection: Gate Access / Security Concerns
body:
Addressing property access and security worries.
- Scoop crews are background-checked and insured.
- We can use gate codes, lockboxes, or open-on-service-day access.
- Every visit includes a gate re-latch photo for proof.
- You can update access info anytime.

title: Full Onboarding Process
body:
What happens after they agree to sign up.
1. Collect service details: dogs, yard size, frequency, areas to clean, and add-ons (deodorize, haul-away, compost routing).
2. Access info: dog temperament, gate codes, special instructions.
3. Payment setup: secure payment method (monthly or per-visit).
4. Schedule first visit: preferred start date, day of week, and time window.
5. Confirmation email with full details and service expectations.

title: Service Add-Ons and Options
body:
Additional services customers can include.
- Deodorize & Sanitize: plant-based enzyme spray added after visits.
- Waste diversion: haul-away or compost routing when partners have capacity.
- Extra dogs and extra areas (front yard, side yard, dog run, fenced area) adjust per-visit pricing.
- One-time deep clean is recommended if the yard has not been cleaned recently.

title: Scheduling and Service Windows
body:
How scheduling works.
- Service day: choose a preferred day of week. We aim for consistent day-of-week routes.
- Time windows: morning, afternoon, or flexible depending on availability.
- First visit: typically 3-7 business days out, depending on route capacity.
- Changes: adjust service day or frequency with notice; same-day changes before 8am are sometimes possible.
- Pauses: going on vacation or need to skip? We can pause billing with a quick heads-up.

title: Payment and Billing Details
body:
How billing and payment works.
- Scooping service uses secure card processing. Choose monthly billing (charged in advance) or per-visit billing (charged after each completed visit).
- Invoices include visit details, photos, and add-ons.
- Premium wellness app subscriptions are billed separately through the app stores on iOS.
- Month-to-month means you can cancel anytime with no fees.

title: Dog Safety and Access Requirements
body:
Information we need about dogs and property access.
- Dog temperament: friendly, fearful, or aggressive? We need to know for safety.
- Dog location during service: inside, separate area, or loose in yard.
- Gate/fence type and access method (code, lockbox, open gate).
- Special instructions: tricky latches, escape risks, areas to avoid, seasonal issues.
